title: Bessie Smith's songs and time of the accident
summary: He recalls her last song and repertoire, and that the accident was around 4:30 or 5 a.m.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: the name, what you get. You remember any of the songs that Bessie sang in particular on that last trip? You mentioned the one song, the last one you sang.
Well, this was my last affair.
The last one. Were there any other blues or any particular songs?

Well, yeah, she sang a lot of blues, of course. She sang a lot of blues, but... She was just saying... She sang a lot of blues, of course, but... She was just saying... She sang the... TV blues. She sang the TV blues. She sang the TV blues.
She sang the TV blues. She sang the Deaf Letter Blues, Pink Slip Blues, One Hour Mama.
Oh yeah, I remember. That's one of the last things I heard her sing. One Hour Mama. One minute papa, I've got no use for you.
That's right. I remember that. Oh, it's another song by Something in the Park. Something in the Park. I forget what it was.
Of course, she made a lot of records of, I guess, a lot of the songs she made records of, she'd sing in her shows then too, people would want to hear.
I've never heard her sing that.

Some of the pop tunes too she'd sing then. When I'd hear at the Harlem Opera House or at the Apollo, she'd usually sing almost always just blues, is about all they wanted to hear. And I liked the blues too, I was happy to hear just blues. I'm going to ask any more about the show. What time did that happen? I mean about Bessie, you know. It was real late at night, you say, wasn't it? No, it was early in the morning.
Well, that's what I mean, yeah.
Early in the morning and four days during the dark.

Yeah, that's right. It was daylight. It should have been at least around about, must have been around about 4.30 or 5 o'clock. Yeah. It was around about that because, you know, how it is, I mean, in the time when it's, it seemed like the fall is coming, you know, how it looks that time of morning. It was just about maybe 4.30 or probably 5 o'clock in the morning.
